title: Umbrella-Sparked Short Circuit Sets Metro Train Ablaze at Taxqueña Terminal, Line 2 Evacuated
detail: Around 10:00 a.m., an umbrella that fell onto the tracks at the Taxqueña terminal of Metro Line 2 caused a short circuit that ignited a small fire in a train car. Station personnel evacuated the terminal as a precaution while STC rolling-stock and transportation staff extinguished the blaze with chemical fire extinguishers. No injuries were reported and service was briefly disrupted before returning to normal. The Metro reiterated its standing warning for riders to secure loose objects, particularly umbrellas, during the rainy season, after Line 3 alone logged 3,558 recorded faults so far in 2026.

title: Eight Detained in Two Cuauhtémoc Raids, Six Identified as Unión Tepito Members Carrying Guns and Drugs
detail: SSC officers carried out two separate operations in the Cuauhtémoc borough on August 24. In Colonia Obrera, surveillance led to the arrest of two men, Isaac 'N' and Sergio 'N', found with a long firearm loaded with four rounds and marijuana. Separately, a fight and pursuit in the Morelos neighborhood and Centro Histórico ended with the arrest of six more suspects — Édgar Ramsés 'N', Marvin 'N', Jeshua Farid 'N', Jean Iván 'N', Neitan Jared 'N', and Yair 'N' — carrying a handgun and envelopes of suspected narcotics. Public Safety Secretary Pablo Vázquez Camacho identified all six as presumed members of La Unión Tepito, the criminal cell at the center of the ongoing turf war with the Anti-Unión faction that has killed 24 people in the Centro Histórico so far in 2026.

title: Brugada Launches 'Pacto Digital CDMX' to Curb Children's Screen Time and Push Digital Rights Law
detail: Jefa de Gobierno Clara Brugada announced the Pacto Digital CDMX, a strategy to reduce risks from excessive phone and screen use among children and adolescents through regulation, digital education, mental-health support, and incentives to restore in-person interaction. She cited data showing 85% of children aged 6-14 in the capital use the internet at least three hours daily, rising to 98% of 12-17-year-olds averaging over five hours, with 134,000 young people reporting cyberbullying. The plan includes a forthcoming Digital Rights Law for Children and Adolescents, a digital-rights charter covering privacy, data protection and algorithmic transparency, school consultations beginning September 17, new rules curbing cellphone use in classrooms, and measures — developed the following day — to prevent AI deepfakes from being weaponized against women.

media.caption: Clara Brugada announces the Pacto Digital CDMX strategy to regulate children's screen time and advance a digital rights law
